title: Things to Do in Old San Juan: Three Stops for a Closer Look
description: Explore Fuente Raíces, La Rogativa and the Cristo Chapel exterior on an Old San Juan outing with practical route and access considerations.
body:
Looking for things to do in Old San Juan beyond moving from one famous photo spot to the next? Fuente Raíces, Plazuela de la Rogativa and the exterior of Capilla del Santo Cristo de la Salud offer three places to spend time with the city’s public art, streets and setting.

This is a smaller outing within Old San Juan. It does not include fort admission or assume that every waterfront connection is open.

1. Begin near Fuente Raíces

Fuente Raíces stands at the waterfront end of Paseo de la Princesa. Discover Puerto Rico’s promenade guide introduces the setting.

Enjoy the sculpture and surrounding space from dry public paving outside the fountain basin. The stop can be worthwhile whether or not the water is running. Give yourself time to appreciate the composition as part of the promenade, rather than stepping straight back into the next part of the walk.

Plan the stop: Stay outside the basin and follow current barriers. This is an exterior visit with no attraction ticket required. Heat and rain can change how comfortable the waterfront feels, so plan the outing around the conditions.

2. Spend time at La Rogativa

Plazuela de la Rogativa is a public square near Caleta de las Monjas, with a sculpture group that gives the place its identity. The official destination listing provides context for the monument and location.

Use the open public paving to enjoy the setting without climbing on or touching the monument. Public art can be a reason to pause and consider a place rather than simply another object to collect in a camera roll.

Plan the stop: Reach the square through open public streets. Do not make a stair shortcut necessary to the plan. Security arrangements near La Fortaleza can affect access, so respect closures and choose another time if the square is unavailable.

3. Look at the Cristo Chapel from the street

Capilla del Santo Cristo de la Salud stands at the southern end of Calle del Cristo. Discover Puerto Rico’s chapel guide identifies the site.

The exterior is enough for this stop. Enjoy its place at the end of the street from safe public paving, without relying on an open gate or an interior visit. A small building can hold your attention differently from the city’s larger landmarks.

Plan the stop: Stay clear of vehicle movement and drops. Chapel access and access to nearby Parque de las Palomas are separate; neither is needed for the suggestion here. Respect the building’s religious purpose.

Check the route before you set off

Begin on Paseo de la Princesa and choose currently open public streets for the connection to La Rogativa and Calle del Cristo. If using the waterfront approach toward Puerta de San Juan, confirm that the approach and gate are open. This plan does not continue along Paseo del Morro to an assumed connection with El Morro.

Read the National Park Service’s current conditions before choosing waterfront routes. Allow about three hours as a flexible planning budget, including pauses and the changes in level through Old San Juan. Uneven surfaces and slopes matter as much as distance.

The three exterior stops require no attraction ticket. Food, transport and fort or museum visits are separate. Bring water, plan breaks and shorten the outing if heat or weather makes the connections uncomfortable.

Make the visit an adventure of your own

SideQuest’s San Juan City Edition includes activities at these Old San Juan locations, adding playful ways to engage with the places around you. Keep the specifics for your visit. Download SideQuest and look for San Juan to add a quest to the day.
